# HolyCrab Agent Tools v0.4.2

This testing version adds business-focused first-use guidance. No tag or GitHub Release has been created for it.

## Highlights

- Guides a new user from installation to account connection, then suggests e-commerce product images, social media ad videos, and product voiceovers. Examples do not ask users to estimate credits or execute automatically.
- Shares onboarding through CLI account/health results, installers, Skill guidance, and MCP instructions without adding commands or tools. The full introduction is limited to the installation conversation.
- Distinguishes a missing login, an unverified active login, and a verified account. Offline doctor, skipped verification, an environment override, and malformed account responses cannot falsely report a ready account.
- Keeps terminal feedback on stderr and emits a single JSON setup result while preserving public account fields. Upload previews and paid-generation confirmation remain separate.
- Adds `HOLYCRAB_INSTALL_REF` for fixed-commit test downloads. Version validation remains independent and strict; official updates clear the temporary reference and still verify SHA-256 and release versions.
- Retains safe uninstall, Windows DPAPI migration, two-stage Agent uploads, and one-shot paid-submission protection from v0.4.1.
- Records the actual Codex/Claude Code client path and installer ownership. Uninstall and online doctor can locate clients outside the current PATH and compare complete MCP commands and arguments. Claude cleanup is restricted to user scope; manual and unrelated registrations are preserved.
- Reports pending Agent-registration cleanup explicitly instead of claiming a complete uninstall. Keeping a pre-existing or shared PATH is informational, not an error.

## Testing and upgrade

The stable installer entrypoints still install the latest published release, not this testing branch. Test users must use a verified fixed commit. Reinstalling preserves local credentials and records; failed installations restore managed program files. The exact Windows PowerShell 5.1 command is included in the native installer smoke test.

Tests use mocks, fixtures, and read-only Generate source. They do not create production tasks or authorizations, upload media, rename groups, or delete online data. Real novice conversations remain a separate manual acceptance check.
